# The gradient homotopy needs a middle term not generated by channel dyads

## Result and precise scope

Keep the complete five-equation ansatz and the checked polynomial Hamiltonian lift. In the gradient gauge

    M_a=-C_mult rho^2(P_D),  P_a=Q_a=0,
    R=C_mult s_D,

there is NO solution for M_b lying in the regular span of operators

    T_i L_ij T_j*,       T_i,T_j in {A0,B0,C0}.       (1)

Here each L_ij is any regular coefficient operator of the required source, determinant and polynomial type, not merely a constant. The adjoints are the determinant-compatible ones from the Clifford note. In particular, the explicit block-Euler annihilator primitive cannot by itself complete this gradient homotopy, nor can arbitrary regular sums of analogous channel dyads.

This is a universal channel exclusion, not an actual-instance rank test. It is conditional on the displayed, already checked choice of M_a and R. It does NOT exclude a different M_a with a different R, and does not evaluate C_mult.

## 1. Every channel dyad kills the Cartan column

Universal isotropy gives separately

    A0* C0=B0* C0=C0* C0=0.

The first two are already checked by exterior multiplication. The last is the c_m^2 coefficient of monad isotropy. Hence every operator (1) annihilates C0 exactly, even with nonconstant regular L_ij.

Equation (2e) in the complete ansatz would therefore become

    C0 P_b+B0 R=0.                                    (2)

It remains to show that this particular equation is impossible. Nonzero component maps alone would not suffice; the following filtration calculation proves it.

## 2. The negative-coordinate filtration separates the two terms

Work universally in the polynomial coordinate algebra of H=V+W and let I=(W) be its negative-coordinate ideal. This is the formal filtration along the entire linear subspace P(V), not evaluation at a selected point.

The complete torus ansatz places P_b in End(A) tensor Sym^2 W: its coordinate coefficients have pure negative degree two. C0 itself does NOT generally vanish at negative-coordinate zero; its constant term is i_v Ctilde. Nevertheless multiplication by P_b gives

    C0 P_b=0 modulo I^2.                              (3)

Write the fixed Cartan coefficient tensor as

    Ctilde:A -> U tensor Lambda^2 V tensor W,
    C0=i_x Ctilde.

For the gradient construction, with ell=w composed with D and the LINEAR polar vector r(v) of the quadratic q0, satisfying v(r(v))=q0(v),

    r(v) wedge i_ell Ctilde(z)=s_D(z) tau.

Thus s_D, and hence R, has EXACT negative degree one. Meanwhile

    B0=i_x(L wedge omega)=M_alg(v) omega-L wedge i_w omega,

so modulo I one has B0=M_alg(v) omega. Equation (2) modulo I^2 would give

    M_alg(v) R=0 in I/I^2.                            (4)

In the compatible determinant frame the universal Clifford identity is

    M_alg(v)^2=chi q0(v) I_U,      chi != 0.

Multiplying (4) by M_alg(v) gives chi q0 R=0. The universal polynomial algebra and its coefficient modules are torsion-free, and q0 is a nonzero polynomial. Therefore (4) forces R=0. Equivalently one may localize at q0, without choosing a value or point. No actual matrix rank is calculated.

## 3. The common gradient source correction is not zero

The actual Cartan tensor Ctilde is nonzero. The polar map v -> r(v) is an isomorphism because q0 is nondegenerate. As the Hamiltonian direction D varies through sl(W), the covectors w composed with D span W*. Consequently, if s_D vanished identically for every direction, then

    r wedge i_ell Ctilde(z)=0

for every r in V, ell in W* and z in A. Wedge pairing V tensor Lambda^2 V -> Lambda^3 V is nondegenerate. Contraction in W is also nondegenerate. These two exact tensor pairings force Ctilde=0, a contradiction.

This argument proves nonzero of the COMPOSITE itself by separation; it does not infer nonzero from its separate legs. Since the already established multiplier C_mult is nonzero, R=C_mult s_D is a nonzero universal tensor. This contradicts the consequence of (2).

One may equivalently retain a single abstract invertible trace-free Hamiltonian D and vary w. No actual smoothing direction or HM coefficient needs to be selected, and the theorem is stated for the full universal family.

## 4. What the exclusion does and does not establish

The remaining construction in this gradient gauge must include a symplectic middle operator whose action on C0 has a nonzero first negative-coordinate term. Such an operator is not in the regular channel-dyad span. A construction from the full Cartan identification Sym^3 W -> Sym^3 U remains possible and is not excluded.

This does not prove that the reverse source term S is nonzero, does not determine any of the remaining three identities, and does not assign a numerical value to C_mult. Allowing coordinate poles would invalidate the degree comparison for P_b and would leave the permitted global polynomial homotopy space, so it is not an alternative inside this statement.

## Reproduction

Run `python verify_gradient_homotopy_nonchannel_obstruction.py`. The script checks the full negative-coordinate degree separation, the universal Clifford implication, the formal dyad annihilation, and injectivity of the contraction-separation test on a generic exterior tensor. Its symbols are universal tensor coefficients, not coefficients of any selected HM source or monad instance. It evaluates no actual source matrix, rank, parameter value, orbit, or local model.

Inputs: UNIVERSAL-MONAD-HOMOTOPY-HAS-FIVE-CHANNEL-EQUATIONS.md and UNIVERSAL-MONAD-CLIFFORD-HOMOTOPY-AND-HAMILTONIAN-DEFECT.md. Both remain unchanged.
